We need propose retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available chemicals, total price <=9999 (we cannot check price but assume buyable). Need to construct route JSON.

Target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need break into precursors. Likely sulfonamide formation: aniline (p-toluidine) reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from aromatic sulfonyl chloride bearing the rest. So step1: sulfonyl chloride + aniline.

The sulfonyl chloride: O=S(=O)(Cl)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 . That's a sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl with side chain (acrylamide with anilide). Could be made by chlorosulfonation of that phenyl (commercial?). Might be expensive.

Alternative: first form amide between aniline and acryloyl chloride then sulfonylate? Actually target has sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl with side chain. So we could first make sulfonyl chloride from 4-(2-((phenyl)amido)vinyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride (maybe not commercial). Another route: start from 4-aminotoluene (p-toluidine) and 4-(2-((phenyl)amido)vinyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride.

We need leaves commercially available: p-toluidine (buyable). The other fragment maybe can be assembled in two steps: start from 4-bromobenzaldehyde? Actually side chain: phenyl-NH-CO-CH=CH- attached to phenyl-sulfonyl. Could make via Heck coupling of a vinyl sulfonyl chloride? Might be complex.

Simplify: Use retrosynthesis tool search for templates? Could search for amide formation: C(=O)N from aniline and acryloyl chloride. So fragment: C=CC(=O)Nc3ccccc3N is an acryloyl anilide with an aniline at other end? Actually it's N-phenyl acryloyl amide with an aniline substituent on phenyl? Wait: Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline (para? Actually it's an aniline with two Ns? "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an extra N attached? That's an aniline with an amino group attached to phenyl (aniline) and also the amide nitrogen attached to that phenyl. So it's a phenyl ring with an NH at position 1 (attached to carbonyl) and another NH at position? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline where both ends have NH? That's a diamino benzene? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an extra NH attached to the same carbon? That seems like a di-amine (para? Actually it's an aniline with an amino substituent at position 1 and another at position? The SMILES indicates N attached to aromatic carbon, then aromatic ring, then N attached to same carbon? Not typical. Might be a phenyl diamine (p-phenylenediamine). So the amide is attached to one amino of p-phenylenediamine.

Thus we could start from p-phenylenediamine (commercial) and acryloyl chloride to make N-acryloyl-p-phenylenediamine (monoacylated). Then attach sulfonyl chloride to the other amine? Actually sulfonyl attaches to p-toluidine, not to that fragment. So final product has sulfonamide linking p-tolyl to phenyl-sulfonyl, and the phenyl-sulfonyl has side chain acryloyl attached to p-phenylenediamine? Wait side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . So the carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl with an NH (the second N). So the phenyl-sulfonyl fragment is attached to acryloyl amide of p-phenylenediamine.

Thus we could make fragment A: p-phenylenediamine + acryloyl chloride -> N-acryloyl-p-phenylenediamine (mono). Then fragment B: phenyl-sulfonyl chloride (with side chain?) Actually we need to attach the acryloyl amide to phenyl-sulfonyl via the carbonyl side chain attached to phenyl (the phenyl is the same as the sulfonyl phenyl). So we need to have phenyl-sulfonyl chloride that also has the acryloyl amide attached at para position? Actually the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So the phenyl ring (c2) has the side chain at para? Not necessarily.

Thus we could start from 4-(2-((p-phenylenediamine)acrylamide) )benzenesulfonyl chloride. That may not be commercial.

Given limited time, maybe propose a 2-step route: Step1: purchase target directly? Not allowed because leaves must be commercially available chemicals, but target not leaf.

We could propose 3-step: 1) p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride (commercial?) maybe 4-(2-((p-phenylenediamine)acrylamide) )benzenesulfonyl chloride is not commercial.

Alternative: Use sulfonylation of p-toluidine with 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) then do Suzuki coupling to attach side chain? Could attach side chain via Heck coupling of vinyl amide onto bromophenyl-sulfonyl? Might be 2 steps.

Given complexity, maybe we can propose route using available reagents: Step1: p-toluidine + 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride -> intermediate sulfonamide (p-tolyl-sulfonyl-4-bromophenyl). Step2: Suzuki coupling with (E)-3-(p-phenylenediamine)acrylamide boronic acid? Not sure.
